title: Verify Prometheus is running and serving metrics

whenTrue.title: Verify Prometheus metrics are written to an endpoint

blocks.content: Installing and configuring Prometheus is out of scope for this path. Before you change its configuration, confirm that Prometheus is running and that it serves metrics. If it isn't, nothing reaches Grafana Cloud after you add `remote_write`, and you'd be troubleshooting the wrong thing.
To verify that Prometheus is running and serving metrics:
Log in to the machine on which Prometheus is installed.
If required, switch to a user that has administrative privileges.

Check the Prometheus service status.

For Linux with systemd:

```
systemctl status prometheus
```

For Windows:

```
sc query prometheus
```

The service should report that it's active or running:

whenTrue.alt: Picture that shows the Prometheus service up and running

blocks.content:
In a browser, open the metrics endpoint of your Prometheus server. By default Prometheus listens on port `9090`.

For example, navigate to `http://localhost:9090/metrics`

This page lists the metrics Prometheus exposes about itself. If it loads, Prometheus is running and reachable:

whenTrue.alt: Picture that shows metrics in a browser tab

blocks.content:
To confirm that Prometheus is also scraping your own targets, navigate to `http://localhost:9090/targets`.

Each target you configured under `scrape_configs` should show the state **UP**. These are the metrics that `remote_write` sends to Grafana Cloud.

**Tip:** If the service isn't running or a target isn't **UP**, fix that first. Refer to the [Prometheus documentation](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/getting_started/) for installation and scrape configuration.
